a25b41ea.title: Carbon dioxide removal pathway
a25b41ea.caption: Cellular respiration produces carbon dioxide. Blood carries it to the lungs; it diffuses from the capillary blood into the alveolar air and leaves during exhalation. The SVG shows the gas-exchange step.

f8b5f8d.title: Urea removal pathway
f8b5f8d.caption: Urea is made in the liver during the processing of excess amino acids. Blood carries it to the kidneys; urea remaining in the urine passes through the ureters to the bladder and leaves through the urethra. The SVG shows the urinary route, not urea production in the liver.

40e3141b.title: Water and salts in sweat removal pathway
40e3141b.caption: Sweat glands form a watery secretion containing dissolved salts. Sweat passes from the coiled gland through its duct to the skin surface. Water and some salts leave the body; evaporation of the water cools the skin. The published SVG shows the gland and duct.

5fb69548.title: Bile pigments removal pathway
5fb69548.caption: Breakdown of haemoglobin from old red blood cells produces bile pigments such as bilirubin. The liver processes bilirubin and secretes it in bile. Bile flows through the bile ducts into the duodenum; intestinal breakdown products leave mainly in faeces. The SVG shows the liver-to-intestine route. Key: RHD = right hepatic duct; LHD = left hepatic duct; CHD = common hepatic duct.

c54173f4.title: Undigested food in faeces removal pathway
steps: Food is digested and nutrients are absorbed
Undigested and unabsorbed material remains in the alimentary canal
Faeces leave through the anus: egestion, not excretion

4f65e2d6.title: Eye anatomy: focusing on a near object
4f65e2d6.caption: For a near object, the ciliary muscles contract, tension in the suspensory ligaments decreases and the lens becomes thicker, increasing refraction. This reference shows the anatomy rather than a measured ray trace.

bc78f401.title: Eye anatomy: focusing on a distant object
bc78f401.caption: For a distant object, the ciliary muscles relax, the suspensory ligaments tighten and the lens becomes thinner, reducing refraction. This reference shows the anatomy rather than a measured ray trace.

c8e1987a.title: Eye anatomy: bright light
c8e1987a.caption: In bright light, the circular muscles of the iris contract and the radial muscles relax. The pupil narrows, reducing the light entering the eye.

62a735ee.title: Eye anatomy: dim light
62a735ee.caption: In dim light, the radial muscles of the iris contract and the circular muscles relax. The pupil widens, allowing more light to enter.
